Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy. Chlorophyll in the chloroplasts absorbs sunlight, primarily in the red and blue wavelengths, and uses it to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen. This process is the foundation of most food chains on Earth, since it is the primary way that solar energy enters biological systems.

The French Revolution began in 1789 and fundamentally transformed French society by dismantling the absolute monarchy and the feudal system. It was driven by widespread frustration with rigid social hierarchies, food shortages, and the crown's near-bankrupt finances after years of costly wars. The revolution eventually gave rise to the Reign of Terror, followed by the rise of Napoleon Bonaparte, who would go on to reshape much of Europe.

Machine learning is a subfield of artificial intelligence focused on building systems that improve their performance on a task through experience, rather than through explicit, hand-written rules. A supervised learning model, for example, is trained on labeled examples and learns to generalize from them so it can make predictions on new, unseen data. Common approaches include decision trees, neural networks, and support vector machines, each with different tradeoffs in interpretability, training cost, and accuracy.

Coffee brewing methods vary widely across cultures, but most rely on the same basic principle: hot water extracts soluble compounds from ground coffee beans. Espresso forces pressurized hot water through finely-ground coffee very quickly, producing a concentrated shot with a layer of crema on top. Pour-over methods, by contrast, use gravity and a slower, more controlled water flow, which tends to produce a cleaner, brighter-tasting cup.
